    39	H.1 Gaining and Losing Hirelings
    40	H.1.1     Gaining from Supply. When a player’s score 
    41	marker enters a space with a hireling marker, they 
    42	take the hireling marker and place it below their 
    43	Evening (as a reminder). At the end of their turn, 
    44	they take any hireling card from the supply, roll for 
    45	control (H.1.2), and flip over the hireling marker.
    46	H.1.2     Rolling for Control. When a player gains a hire­
    47	ling card, they roll the control die and place con­
    48	trol markers on the hireling card equal in number 
    49	to the die roll. They count only the gold die pips 
    50	if they have the most victory points or are tied for 
    51	the most; they count all the die pips otherwise (in­
    52	cluding if they have activated a dominance card).
    53	H.1.3     Gaining from Another Player. At the end of a 
    54	player’s turn, they must remove one control mark­
    55	er from each hireling card they gained on previ­
    56	ous turns. Then, they must give each hireling card 
    57	they control that has no control markers, along 
    58	with a hireling marker, to any other player (even 
    59	the player with the highest score). That player puts the 
    60	hireling marker below their Evening (as a remind­
    61	er) and immediately rolls for control (H.1.2).

    63	Hirelings have various actions and abilities, as shown 
    64	by unique icons. Actions and abilities that start with

    67	). When they take con­
    68	trol of the hireling, the controlling player must 
    69	take this action.  
    70	H.2.2     Ability (
    71	). This ability is always active or it 
    72	specifies when it happens.
    73	H.2.3     Start-of-Birdsong Action (
    74	). At the start of 
    75	their Birdsong, the controlling player must or 
    76	may take this action, as the action describes.
    77	H.2.4     Once-Per-Daylight Action (
    78	). Once in their 
    79	Daylight, the controlling player may take this action.
    80	H.3 Rules
    81	H.3.1     Rule. A hireling’s controller treats hireling piec­
    82	es as their own only for rule. (The controller can 
    83	rule a clearing even with hirelings alone.) Uncon­
    84	trolled hirelings can rule clearings as if they were 
    85	players (2.5).
    86	H.3.2     Enemy Status. A hireling is an enemy to players 
    87	other than its controller and players in coalition 
    88	with its controller.
    89	H.3.3     Separate Pieces. Hireling pieces are not the con­
    90	troller’s faction pieces. (So, the Duchy cannot count 
    91	them as Duchy pieces to sway, the Keepers cannot re­
    92	move them to encamp, etc.). 
    93	H.3.4     Separate Actions. A hireling’s Move or Battle ac­
    94	tions can only move or battle with the hireling’s 
    95	pieces and cannot include the controller’s pieces. 
    96	Hirelings cannot take actions in other ways (such 
    97	as from their controller’s Move actions, False Orders, or 
    98	the Vagabond’s Allied Relationship).
    99	H.3.5     Separate Effects. Hirelings cannot use their con­
   100	troller’s abilities, crafted persistent effects, or am­
